text:
This change adds `pointsFor`, which turns an order into whole-euro points, and `creditOrders`, which adds each order's points to a `points:<customerId>` balance in the key-value `Store`. It also adds tests for both. I found one bug that should block the merge, plus a gap in the tests that hides it.

**Two orders from the same customer lose points.** `creditOrders` starts every `addPoints` call at once with `Promise.all`. Each call reads the balance, waits, then writes balance + points back. The `Store` interface (`src/store.ts`) only has `get` and `set`: there is no atomic increment and no transaction. So when one batch holds two orders from the same customer, both calls read the same starting balance before either one writes. The last write wins and the other order's points are lost.

For example, Ana has 3 points and two 10-euro orders in the batch. Both calls read 3 and both write 13, so she ends with 13 instead of 23. A batch of orders often holds more than one order per customer, so this would lose customers' points without any error.

**The test can't catch this.** The test for `creditOrders` gives each customer exactly one order, so the calls never touch the same key. Its in-memory store also resolves `get` almost at once. A test with two orders for the same customer would show the lost update.

None of the repository's rules is broken. Amounts stay in integer cents, nothing is logged and no SQL is built.
